attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “This is an instance of ordinary parallel repetition [14].” Its bibliography: “[14] Ran Raz. A parallel repetition theorem. SIAM Journal on Computing, 27(3):763–803, 1998. doi:10.1137/S0097539795280895.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Theorem 2.3 (Uniform parallel repetition) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of Min-UnCut” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-Min-UnCut-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3300408a7ae8900e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an effectively specified constant c < 1 such that every finite game with at most eight first-player answers, at most two second-player answers, and value at most 11/12 has r-fold repeated value at most cr for all integers r ≥ 0. The same c works for all question distributions and all question-set sizes.
